title: Advances and Perspectives of Mexican Microscopy, Part II: Biological Sciences
content: In México, the use of microscopy has maintained a progressive trend towards increasing its role in education [1], dissemination, and research activities in biological and materials sciences. In this paper, we focus on what is related to the Biological Sciences. The Mexican Association of Microscopy and Microanalysis (AMMM) (https://www.ammmicro.mx/), have joined efforts to coordinate especially educational and dissemination activities, with the participation of researchers that benefit from the application of microscopy techniques to their investigations, all over México. The AMMM organizes the Mexican Congress on Microscopy every two years (https://www.ammmicro.mx/congreso/). As a member of the CIASEM and IFSM, it has organized some Interamerican Congresses on Microscopy (1993, 2001, 2011, 2022) and the XVI International Congress on Electron Microscopy (1998). The AMMM focuses its activities on the organization of seminars, talks, and courses etc. More recently it is publishing the MICRO-X bulletin (https://www.ammmicro.mx/bulletin/) (Fig. 1A). The areas that are cultivated in México include: cellular and molecular biology, natural resources and biodiversity, agricultural sciences, neurosciences, pathology, forensic science, bionanotechnology, parasitology, environmental sciences, dental science, education on microscopy, among others.
